input: The two groups under discussion report lifetime values for the benchmark material that are in clear conflict, the difference between them being considerably larger than the scatter either group reports within its own results. On examination, the disagreement is located in the conditions under which the ageing was carried out rather than in the material itself. The first of the groups ages the material in a dry feed and reports the lifetime as the time taken for the capacity to fall to a stated fraction of its initial value, whereas the second group ages the material in a humid feed and reports the lifetime to the same fractional loss. Since water competes for the same sites that the separation itself makes use of, a humid feed represents the harder duty of the two, and the shorter lifetime reported by the second group is in the direction that would be expected on that basis. A further difference is that the second group regenerates the material more severely between cycles, which is a second respect in which its conditions press harder on the lifetime. Both groups employ IAST in reducing their mixture measurements, so that the difference between the two reports cannot be put down to a difference in the manner in which the measurements have been treated. The preference that emerges is a limited one: where the duty under consideration carries water in the feed, the value of the second group is the more appropriate guide, since it was obtained under the condition that governs the application, whilst on a dried feed the value of the first group is the closer guide, and it is on this correspondence of conditions, rather than on any judgement as to which group is in general more reliable, that the preference rests.
target: Reported lifetimes for the benchmark material conflict: the difference between the two groups' values is larger than the scatter either group reports, and the disagreement sits in the test conditions rather than in the material. One group ages the material in a dry feed and reports the lifetime as the time to a stated fractional loss of capacity. The other ages it in a humid feed and reports the lifetime to the same fractional loss. Water competes for the same sites the separation uses, so the humid feed is the harder duty, and the second group's shorter lifetime is in the expected direction. The second group also regenerates the material more severely between cycles, a second respect in which its conditions press harder on lifetime. Both groups use IAST in reducing their mixture measurements, so the difference between the reports is not a difference of reduction method. The preference is limited, and it rests on a stated condition. Where the duty in view carries water in the feed, the humid-feed value is the closer guide, because it was measured under the condition that governs the application. On a dried feed, the dry-feed value is the closer guide, and the longer lifetime it reports is not evidence against the humid-feed value. Neither value transfers to a duty whose feed condition matches neither test, and a lifetime quoted without its feed condition carries no usable information.
